F1.evidence: Manifest skills, active surface, recursive runtime closure, and host-neutral public instructions are executable and classified.

F2.evidence: An opaque installed runtime completes separate start/status/resume/doctor turns and SPEC to RESULT using only consumer-local state. Lower-level controller cases separately prove arbitrary hook/plugin environment parity and non-destructive corruption, lock, and ambiguity handling.
commands: env -u HARNESS_HOOKS -u CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT -u PYTHONPATH python3 -m pytest tests/e2e/test_codex_harness_acceptance.py::test_clean_environment_controller_plan_to_result_and_recorded_outcomes -q

F3.evidence: A real consumer-owned loopback Chrome CDP test imports the same ECMAScript-valid Panel.tsx, observes computed-visible Ready/false, dispatches a coordinate click to the actual button, and observes computed-visible Complete/true; shared explicit verify passes on the same changed file before RESULT. A no-op handler with old expected literals/test-id retained in comments still fails behaviorally and blocks RESULT. Browser unavailable, consumer behavior failure, shared-gate failure, default-branch, missing-E2E, and secret failures are non-skipping failures. This is rendered DOM/computed visibility/click evidence, not pixel or screenshot parity. Lower-level cases cover explicit/worktree/hook parity, assignment/JSON/Bearer forms, and expired or malformed allowlists.

F4.evidence: A schema-valid test-owned sole-writer simulation validates worker envelopes and appends engineer/compliance/review/test, retry, escalation-open, and explicit USER resolution events. It is not claimed as a production orchestrator API. Its incomplete task table makes the production controller block RESULT; resolved stages plus executable gate PASS evidence permit RESULT.

F5.evidence: One E2E collection produces SAFE_FIX, justified REJECTED, and ESCALATED dispositions; unresolved escalation or a failed local command prevents convergence, while exact user resolution plus build/lint/test success converges. Lower-level cases prove strict malformed-input rejection, edited/reopened revision redisposition, and audit lock/I/O failure closure.

F6.evidence: The same explicit learning policy returns APPLY for a canonical project file and proposal-only for a protected harness file without automatic mutation. Lower-level cases separately cover traversal, absolute/NUL input, out-of-root symlink alias, and broken-link containment.

F7.evidence: The installed adapter distinguishes unavailable, not-initialized, and healthy graph states; fallback is explicitly approximate and does not claim call relationships.

F8.evidence: Trusted-local audit retains raw review evidence only below .harness/audit, while CLI/report and this result evidence are redacted; unconfigured knowledge sync is SKIPPED and no external destination is written.

F9.evidence: The deterministic offline train and held-out fixture runner is collected by pytest; live eval remains an explicit non-pytest command.

F10.evidence: Active role profiles share host-neutral result/ownership contracts. The test-owned sole-writer simulation validates those envelope fields and creates authoritative fixture events; production controller transition authority is verified separately and is not attributed to the simulator.

limitations.reason: Hosted CI required checks, remote head identity, provider posting, export, and sharing are outside the trusted-local baseline and require explicit external configuration.
